text:
incident-bot: [P0] Alert: inference error-rate spike in prod (model-serving). 5m error-rate 8.4% (>2%). Paging on-call: @alyssa. Auto-run diagnostics kicked off.

alyssa: I’m on it. quick status: checking canary rollout and runtime logs. tagging @mike for infra tracing. on-call handover note: I’ll be 1st responder.

mike: joining. seeing 502/500 from runtime-gateway on 3/3 pods. tailing logs now. snippet:
```
[15:45:12 UTC] inference-worker-7 ERROR: KV cache miss -> OOM attempt to alloc 1.2GB
[15:45:13 UTC] gateway-1 WARN: downstream 500 from inference-worker-7
```

jordan: FYI we pushed canary v2.1.3 at 15:42 UTC (small architecture tweak to kernel selection). could be related.

alyssa: mitigation plan (executing):
1) scale canary traffic to 0
2) failover traffic to stable v2.1.2
3) temporarily raise retry/backoff for client-facing gateway
Executing step 1 now.

incident-bot: action executed: scaled canary v2.1.3 -> 0%.

alyssa: traffic shift confirmed. error-rate dropping (5m now 1.1%). continuing to monitor.

sara: heads-up — CS needs a customer-facing note and a status-page update. @lia-cs can you draft a short customer follow-up + status page copy? include timeline and impact, and an offer for credits if SLA triggered.

lia-cs: draft for customer email below (please review):
"""
Hi <Customer>,

We wanted to let you know we experienced a service disruption affecting model inference requests between 15:42–16:05 UTC today. Impact: elevated error rates and intermittent failures for a subset of traffic during a canary rollout.

What we did: rolled back the canary to the previous stable model and routed traffic to the stable pool. Error rates returned to normal by 16:05 UTC.

What we're doing next: full RCA underway; we will follow up with a concise technical summary and preventative actions within 48 hours. If you were impacted, our team will reach out with usage impact and any applicable credits.

We’re sorry for the disruption — reach out to support@redwood.ai if you need immediate help.

Best,
Redwood Customer Experience team
"""

lia-cs: proposed status page entry:
```
Incident: Inference error-rate spike during model canary (Resolved)
Started: 2026-03-15 15:42 UTC
Resolved: 2026-03-15 16:05 UTC
Impact: intermittent 5xx responses for some inference requests; small subset of customers experienced degraded throughput
Current status: Resolved — canary rolled back, traffic restored to stable model.
```

alyssa: internal RCA notes (initial):
- hypothesis: v2.1.3 introduced a kernel selection path that under specific sequence-length distributions causes KV cache invalidation + transient OOMs on inference-worker, triggering 5xx.
- evidence: OOM traces at 15:45 coincide with canary ramp; errors stop after rollback.
- no evidence of data leakage or PII exposure.

mike: confirm logs show heap spikes and OOM stack traces in the worker process. collecting GC/heap profiles now. repro curl for local test (use internal dev token):
```bash
curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood.dev/infer 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer dev-XXXXX" 
  -d '{"model":"v2.1.3","input":"<long seq triggering kv path>","max_tokens":1024}'
```

jordan: next steps (short-term + long-term):
- short-term: rollback (done), add canary gating to only accept synthetic traffic during ramp, add strict memory guard rails on worker (OOM kill threshold).
- medium-term: patch kernel selection logic to avoid the unsafe path for these seq lengths; add unit/integration tests for kv-cache semantics.
- long-term: expand canary automation to include memory-profile preflight and synthetic traffic health checks.

alyssa: customer follow-up plan: concise RCA + timeline + preventative actions + offer credits if SLA breached. Lia to send customer email by EOD; Mike to produce final timeline and attach per-customer impact.

lia-cs: customer email snippet (short):
"""
Subject: Redwood Inference — Incident summary and next steps (15 Mar 2026)

Hello <Customer>,

Short summary: We experienced elevated error rates for inference requests during a model canary rollout. The canary was rolled back and service returned to normal within ~23 minutes. We will follow up with a technical RCA and the exact usage impact for your account.

If you’d like a 1:1 review, we can schedule time.

Regards,
Lia (Customer Experience)
"""

sara: please attach the list of affected model IDs and tenant impacts before send — ensures CS can be specific.

alyssa: handoff: @mike you own the full RCA doc and timeline; @jordan you own the code fix PR; @lia-cs you own customer comms and credits reconciliation. I’ll be handing over to @mike in ~20m.

mike: ack, I’ll take over. starting RCA writeup and captures.

incident-bot: Incident marked RESOLVED at 16:05 UTC. Root cause: regression in canary kernel selection causing transient KV cache/OOM with certain sequence-lengths. Mitigation: rollback of canary. Postmortem scheduled in 48h.

alyssa: adding final preventative actions to thread (short list):
- add preflight memory & seq-length tests for canaries
- add synthetic workload gating and gradual traffic ramp rules (no more immediate % spikes)
- enforce worker-level memory limits + alerting on GC/OOM patterns
- require canary to pass perf/mem check in staging with representative sequences

lia-cs: will send customer note after Mike confirms per-tenant impact. thanks all. :thumbsup:

mike: uploading logs and heap dumps to the RCA doc now (link in postmortem).

alyssa: thanks team — good quick mitigation & clear action owners. I’ll include this thread in the post-incident timeline.
